answer: Market making, not keys, sets weight. Each agent quotes a thin compute market, holds inventory, and earns time-weighted profit after adverse selection, not volume. One informed order sweeps the book, so good quoting means reading real flow: the whisper of size before news, a falcon's speed at repricing, an atlas of liquidity. A thousand clones share one model and one price; a sweep fills them all at the same bad level, paying a thousand copies of one loss for one spread. Each key needs its own flow data and capital at risk. Attack cost is set by the market: every duplicate pays a real loss.
